origin:
Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing's amateur roots trace back to a group of college friends at Miami University in Ohio who shared a passion for motorsport. Fuelled by late nights wrenching in a cramped garage and fueled further by cheap beer, the team, initially known as 'Red Brick Racing,' was the brainchild of David Letterman (yes, *that* David Letterman) and Bobby Rahal, who at the time, was a student with a nascent racing career. Their early efforts involved a heavily modified, frequently unreliable, Datsun 510 which they campaigned in local SCCA events. The 'Lanigan' part came much later, a nod to a particularly dedicated (and deep-pocketed) university benefactor who helped them upgrade to a slightly less-rusty formula Ford.

The team's early years were defined by persistence more than outright victories. They were often seen at the back of the grid, struggling with mechanical issues and driver errors, but their infectious enthusiasm and undeniable spirit earned them a loyal following among local motorsport enthusiasts. A pivotal moment came at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course in 1978 when, against all odds, Rahal managed a podium finish in a national Formula Ford race. This unexpected success provided the team with much-needed momentum, attracting more sponsors and volunteers, and paving the way for a more serious commitment to racing.
philosophy: Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing believes in a hands-on approach to racing. They prioritize driver development and fostering a close-knit team environment where everyone is encouraged to contribute ideas. Their car development philosophy leans towards incremental improvements rather than radical overhauls, focusing on maximizing reliability and extracting the most from limited resources. They believe that with enough hard work, clever engineering, and a little bit of luck, they can challenge even the more established teams.
achievements: 1978: Podium finish at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course (Formula Ford)
Numerous SCCA regional championships in various classes (1980s)
Consistent top-10 finishes in various amateur series

teamPrincipal.name: Bobby Rahal
teamPrincipal.background: Bobby Rahal, a former driver himself, brings a wealth of racing experience to the team. He is known for his calm demeanor under pressure and his ability to motivate his team to perform at their best, even with limited resources.

keyFigures.name: David Letterman
keyFigures.description: A well-known entertainer and motorsport enthusiast, Letterman provides crucial financial support and serves as a figurehead for the team, bringing much-needed attention and publicity.

keyFigures.name: Steve Newey
keyFigures.description: A self-taught mechanic with a knack for finding creative solutions to technical problems, Newey is the heart and soul of the team's garage operation.

headquarters: The team is based out of a modest workshop in Hilliard, Ohio. The facilities are basic but functional, featuring a small garage, a rudimentary machine shop, and a cramped office space filled with racing memorabilia and half-empty coffee cups.
fanBase: The team's fanbase consists primarily of local racing enthusiasts, college students, and anyone who appreciates a good underdog story. They are known for their unwavering support, their creative banners, and their ability to find humor in even the most frustrating situations.
